# `silk/char`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.

Checked construction, integer inspection, equality, and ordering for Unicode scalar `char`
values.

## When to use

Prefer comparison operators in direct expressions. Import these functions when comparison must
be passed by name or when the Unicode scalar ordering should be explicit at a call site.

## Details

Ordering compares scalar values, not locale collation, normalization, grapheme clusters, or UTF-8
byte sequences. These functions allocate no storage and add no Effect channels.

## Gotchas

Integer construction rejects `0xD800` through `0xDFFF` and values above `0x10FFFF`. It returns
`None`; it does not truncate or trap.

## Examples

### Validate a Unicode scalar integer

```silk
import silk.char

import silk.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let scalar = char.fromU32(0x2603)
  let value = move scalar
    |> Option<char>.unwrapOr('?')
  if char.toU32(value) != 0x2603 {
    return 1
  }
  let surrogate = char.fromU32(0xD800)
  let replacement = move surrogate
    |> Option<char>.unwrapOr('?')
  if replacement != '?' {
    return 2
  }
  return 42
}
```
